case_title.correct_value: Sham @ Kishor Bhaskarrao Matkari v. State of Maharashtra
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.reason: A single appellant-accused is before the Court.

accused_gender.quote: he was sleeping with the other victims in the same house
accused_gender.reason: The judgment refers to the accused with male pronouns and as the brother of the deceased.

accused_age.quote: the accused was 28 years old and was jobless
accused_age.reason: The Court states the accused's age at the time of the incident as 28. Page 16 gives 38 as a mitigation plea, which the Court did not adopt.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.quote: the accused was 28 years old and was jobless
accused_occupation.reason: The judgment says the accused was jobless at the time of the incident.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth or class; joblessness alone is captured in occupation.

previous_criminal_record.quote: the antecedents of the accused-appellant are unblemished as nothing is shown by the prosecution
previous_criminal_record.reason: The Court records unblemished antecedents and no prior criminal activity shown.

victim_gender.quote: his wife, Meena (since deceased) and three children, namely, Akhilesh (since deceased), Monika (PW-7) and Vishwesh
victim_gender.reason: Victims include male and female family members, including a daughter and sons.

victim_age.reason: The judgment gives no victim ages, only describing the daughter as a minor girl.

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community of the victims is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religious identity of the victims is stated.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: The quarrel started due to the land dispute
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Brothers sharing a household, with a land dispute the Court accepted as the quarrel's source.

offence_category.quote: the murders were neither pre-meditated nor pre-planned
offence_category.reason: Main conviction is murder under s.302 IPC, with s.307 as an attempt.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s.302; IPC s.307; IPC s.201 (acquitted at trial)
statutory_provisions.quote: for the offence punishable under Section 302 IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Crime was registered under ss.302, 307 and 201; s.201 conviction was not upheld.

weapon.correct_value: None mentioned as a dangerous weapon; a large stone and gas cylinder were found near the body
weapon.quote: No weapon much less a dangerous weapon was used in commission of offence
weapon.reason: Court states no dangerous weapon was used and records the stone and cylinder found near the body.

evidence_type.quote: There is no reason to disbelieve the version of PW-7
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, post-mortem medical opinion, stone recovery and confession are all relied on.

confession.correct_value: Statement to Executive Magistrate (PW-16) treated under s.164 CrPC; not a dying declaration; relied on
confession.quote: Though the said statement is not a dying declaration, however, the accused knowing all the seriousness confessed
confession.reason: Matches the Court's treatment of the confession as relied upon and not a dying declaration.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Three deaths and injuries to two children; victims asleep; brutality; High Court's list of aggravating circumstances
aggravating_circumstances.quote: The assault on victims by the respondent was aimed at midnight when the victims were fast asleep
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Facts match the High Court's listed aggravating circumstances the Court discussed.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: No pre-plan; land dispute; no dangerous weapon; unblemished antecedents; age 28 and jobless; long custody
mitigating_circumstances.quote: he had no pre-plan to do away with the family of his brother
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Each listed mitigating factor is noted in the judgment's discussion.

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: s.302: life imprisonment and Rs.25,000 fine; s.307: 7 years RI and Rs.1,000 fine; s.201: acquitted
trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced him to imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/-
trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the trial court sentences and acquittal under s.201 stated in the judgment.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Accused's appeal dismissed; State's appeal allowed; life sentence enhanced to death
high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court dismissed the appeal filed by the appellant-accused and allowed the appeal filed by the State and enhanced the sentence
high_court_outcome.reason: Matches the High Court's disposal of both appeals.

final_outcome.quote: while maintaining the conviction of the appellant-accused for the offence under Section 302 IPC
final_outcome.reason: Conviction was upheld and life sentence restored; the sentence is the trial court's, so 'convicted' fits better than 'conviction_modified'.

imprisonment_type.quote: we restore the sentence of life imprisonment as directed by the trial Court
imprisonment_type.reason: Final sentence restored is life imprisonment.

imprisonment_years.reason: Final sentence is life imprisonment, not a fixed term.

fine_rs.correct_value: 25000 (s.302 fine per trial court; SC did not expressly restate fine)
fine_rs.quote: to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/-, in default of payment of fine, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for two years
fine_rs.reason: Restored trial sentence likely carried the Rs.25,000 fine, though the Court does not expressly restate it.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Same summary with 'he' replaced (e.g. 'said that he would deal' rewritten as 'said the victim would be dealt with later')
neutral_facts.quote: during which the accused said he would deal with the victim later
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate and do not reveal outcome, but the gendered pronoun 'he' breaches the no-gender-pronoun rule.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not expressly state the statutory maximum or minimum for s.302.

attempt_completion.quote: three persons were done to death
attempt_completion.reason: Main offence is completed murder; the attempt under s.307 is secondary, so the single value should be Completed.

physical_harm.correct_value: Death of brother, sister-in-law and son; injuries to two children; wife partly burnt
physical_harm.quote: Meena was partially burnt and a stone of big size and a gas cylinder with tube were lying near her body
physical_harm.reason: Deaths, child injuries and partial burning are all described in the judgment.

number_of_offences.quote: registered being Crime No. 41 of 2001 for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 307 and 201
number_of_offences.reason: Three sections charged; ss.302 and 307 upheld, s.201 acquitted at trial.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss is established; the claimed theft by thieves was found false.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Not found by Supreme Court; High Court had found premeditation
premeditation_planning.quote: he had no pre-plan to do away with the family of his brother
premeditation_planning.reason: Supreme Court found no pre-plan; High Court's contrary finding is recorded accurately.

motive.quote: Only on account of property dispute, the appellant went to the extent of committing murders
motive.reason: Court accepted the land/property dispute as the motive.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Eyewitness evidence of PW-7, PWs 1 and 3; medical opinion of PWs 6 and 11; stone recovery; confession to Executive Magistrate
key_evidence_accepted.quote: Considering the opinion of the doctors, (PWs-6 and 11), cause of death and recovery of a stone
key_evidence_accepted.reason: The evidence listed is the evidence the Court relied on.

witness_credibility.correct_value: Found credible; no reason to disbelieve PW-7, PWs 1 and 3, and the confession
witness_credibility.quote: There is no reason to disbelieve the version of Monika (PW-7)
witness_credibility.reason: Court expressly found no reason to disbelieve these witnesses.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Gave false thieves story; found with blood on hands and clothes; High Court found story false
post_offence_conduct.quote: the accused told that three thieves entered into their house
post_offence_conduct.reason: Conduct and the High Court's finding that the story was false are both noted in the judgment.

custody_duration.correct_value: In jail since 30.06.2001; in death cell since 03.05.2006
custody_duration.quote: He is in jail since 30.06.2001 and in the death cell since the date of the judgment of the High Court
custody_duration.reason: Matches the dates given; 'over 10' and 'over 5 years' are the Court's own characterisations.

bail_history.reason: No bail grant or refusal is mentioned in the judgment.

trial_duration.correct_value: offence: 28/29.06.2001; trial judgment: 04/05.03.2003; High Court: 03.05.2006; Supreme Court: 30.09.2011
trial_duration.reason: All dates match those stated in the judgment.

legal_representation.correct_value: Accused: Tara Chand Sharma, Mahabir Singh Mangla, Uma Datta, Kishan Datta, Neelam Sharma. State: Sushil Karanjkar, Sachin Patil, Sanjay Kharde, Sankar A Chillarge, Asha Gopalan Nair
legal_representation.quote: Tara Chand Sharma, Mahabir Singh Mangla, Uma Datta, Kishan Datta and Neelam Sharma for the Appellant
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names match the appearance listing.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered; investigation completed; accused arrested; charge-sheet laid; trial completed
investigation_status.quote: A crime was registered being Crime No. 41 of 2001
investigation_status.reason: Each investigation step is described in the judgment.

procedural_irregularity.reason: The Court notes no procedural lapse.

appeal_history.correct_value: Trial: life for s.302, 7 years for s.307. HC: accused's appeal dismissed, State's allowed, death imposed. SC: conviction upheld, death set aside, life restored
appeal_history.quote: dismissed the appeal preferred by the appellant-accused and allowed the appeal preferred by the State
appeal_history.reason: Outcome at each level matches the judgment.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Death justified given three deaths and injuries to two children; relied on Ajitsingh Hamamsingh Gujral
prosecution_argument.quote: in view of death of three persons and causing injuries to two, all in one family, the High Court was justified
prosecution_argument.reason: Matches the State's submissions as recorded.

defence_argument.correct_value: Mitigating circumstances mean death not warranted; not rarest of rare
defence_argument.quote: in view of several mitigating circumstances highlighted before the High Court
defence_argument.reason: Matches the defence submissions recorded by the Court.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Rarest of rare test; weighing aggravating and mitigating circumstances per Bachan Singh and later cases
legal_principle_applied.quote: This Court, in series of decisions has indicated various aggravating and mitigating circumstances
legal_principle_applied.reason: Principle applied matches the Court's stated approach.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Ajitsingh Hamamsingh Gujral, JT 2011 (10) SC 465 (distinguished); Bachan Singh (1980) 2 SCC 684; Machhi Singh (1983) 3 SCC 470; C. Muniappan (2010) 9 SCC 567
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Ajitsingh Hamamsingh Gujral vs. State of Maharashtra, JT 2011 (10) SC 465 - distinguished
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Case names and citations match those in the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Not a rarest of rare case; High Court gave inadequate reasons; trial court's life sentence restored
sentencing_rationale.quote: it is not a rarest of rare case where extreme penalty of death is called for
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale matches the Court's reasoning for restoring life imprisonment.

judicial_mitigating_factors.correct_value: No pre-plan; land dispute; no dangerous weapon; unblemished antecedents; reformable; not a menace; trial court's demeanour assessment
judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: the trial Court which had the opportunity of noting demeanour of all the witnesses
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Each factor is weighed by the Court in its reasoning.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Three deaths; no other aggravating factor weighed
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: Though the appellant caused death of three persons
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The Court acknowledges three deaths and does not weigh other aggravating factors.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or guidelines are ordered.
